what_it_does: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) allows computation on encrypted data so private inputs never need to be exposed — useful for running AI models in the cloud on sensitive data. The problem is translating a standard neural network (like those built in PyTorch) into FHE operations, because FHE has strict rules: data must be packed into large fixed-length vectors, and the encryption accumulates 'noise' that must be periodically reset by a very expensive operation called bootstrapping. Existing FHE tools struggle with large, modern networks because the packing problem and bootstrapping placement become combinatorially explosive. Orion is an automated compiler that accepts a normal PyTorch network and produces a working FHE program. It uses a single-pass packing strategy that efficiently places convolutional filter data into FHE vectors without the explosion of earlier methods, and automatically finds the cheapest positions to insert bootstrapping operations by tracking how quickly noise builds up through the layers. The paper claims it handles genuinely large networks — including a 139-million-parameter object-detection model — that prior FHE tools could not compile.
